'''Andrés Marcelo Nocioni''' (born 30 November 1979) is an Argentine former professional [[basketball]] player. He was a two-time [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague selection]] before spending eight seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), from 2004 to 2012. Nocioni won a [[EuroLeague]] title in [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|2015]], earning the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]] Award in the process.

Nocioni was a member of [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]]'s gold medal-winning team at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]] in [[Athens]],<ref name="BBCsports">[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/low/olympics_2004/basketball/3609090.stm Argentina defeats Italy 84-69 to win the men's basketball gold medal] Retrieved September 3, 2006</ref> as well as the Argentina squads that won the bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/BK/C73/BKM400102.shtml |title=Men's Bronze Medal Game - Game 75 |website=Beijing2008.cn |publisher=[[The Beijing Organizing Committee for the Games of the XXIX Olympiad]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080827131536/http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/INF/BK/C73/BKM400102.shtml |archive-date=2008-08-27 |access-date=October 27, 2008}}</ref> and the silver medal at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship|2002 FIBA World Championship in Indianapolis]]. In 2010 he won the [[Konex Award]] as one of the five best Basketball Players from the last decade in Argentina.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/b4213-andres-nocioni|title=Andrés Nocioni - Premio Konex: Diploma al Mérito 2010|language=es}}</ref> His jersey number 13 was retired by the Argentinian Basketball Confederation.<ref name=thirteen/>

==Personal life==
Andrés was the second son of Pedro José "Pilo" Nocioni and Ángela Palmira Roux, both siblings born in Santa Fe although the family lived in [[Gálvez, Santa Fe|Gálvez]], 80 km south of Santa Fe, where Andrés attended school.<ref>[http://www.andreschapunocioni.com/cha-biografia.html#bio03 Biography at Nocioni's official site] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081012053357/http://www.andreschapunocioni.com/cha-biografia.html#bio03 |date=October 12, 2008 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref> Andrés and his wife, fellow Argentine Paula Raquel Aimonetto, have two sons, Laureano<ref name="NBA">[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andres_nocioni/bio.html Nocioni's NBA profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071216083925/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andres_nocioni/bio.html |date=December 16, 2007 }} Retrieved November 27, 2007</ref> and Benicio. Nocioni is known as "Chapu" after the children's TV series ''[[El Chapulín Colorado]]'', which was very popular in Argentina.<ref name="ESPN1000">[http://www.am1000.com/listingsEntry.asp?ID=325718&PT=Silvy+%26+Carmen ESPN 1000-WMVP-AM, explaining Nocioni's nickname of Chapu] Retrieved September 3, 2006  {{dead link|date=May 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He holds Argentine and Italian citizenships.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/columns/story?columnist=hollinger_john&page=All-World-30Best&lpos=spotlight&lid=tab3pos1 |title=The 30 best international players in the NBA |first=John |last=Hollinger |publisher=ESPN |date=April 27, 2007 |access-date=2007-04-28}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Argentina and Spain===
Nocioni's professional career began in the [[Liga Nacional de Básquetbol|Argentine basketball league]] (LNB) in the 1995–96 season in [[Racing Club de Avellaneda]], and in 1998–99 he was already named ''Best Sixth Man''. In 2001, Nocioni went to [[Vitoria-Gasteiz]], where he spent three seasons as a ''refuerzo'' (reinforcement player) with Spain's [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Cerámica]] of the top-tier level [[Liga ACB|ACB Spanish professional league]]. He was the league's 2004 [[ACB Most Valuable Player Award|Most Valuable Player]], and his stellar play earned him an [[All-EuroLeague]] Second Team selection in 2003 and 2004.

===NBA career===
===Chicago Bulls===
After winning the gold medal at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Olympics]], Nocioni was signed as an [[undrafted]] rookie free-agent by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Two of his countrymen, [[Manu Ginóbili]] and [[Carlos Delfino]], were also in the [[NBA]] at the time.

He played in 81 games during his rookie season and posted averages of 8.3 ppg, 4.8 rpg, 1.5 apg and 23.4 mpg.<ref name="NBAplayerBio">[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andres_nocioni/index.html Player stats] Retrieved August 15, 2006</ref> Nocioni's physical style of defense created controversy around the league, and he was suspended for one game after a hard foul to [[Detroit Pistons]]' [[Tayshaun Prince]].<ref name="suspend">{{cite news |title=Chicago Sun-Times article on Nocioni being suspended |date=April 13, 2005 |work=Chicago Sun-Times |via=[[FindArticles]] |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4155/is_20050413/ai_n14595223 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080522091008/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qn4155/is_20050413/ai_n14595223 |archive-date=May 22, 2008 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> Nocioni had previously committed a hard foul on the [[Miami Heat]]'s [[Dwyane Wade]] and then was shoved past photographers and into the first row of spectators by [[Udonis Haslem]]. A spectator tossed a drink at Nocioni, which was similar to the incident that triggered [[Pacers–Pistons brawl]] at [[The Palace of Auburn Hills]]. The fan was ejected by security. For the incident, Nocioni received a flagrant-one foul (which is a foul involving excessive or unjustified contact) and a [[technical foul|technical]]. Haslem received a technical and an [[ejection (sports)|ejection]].<ref name="ChiSport">[http://chicagosports.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/cs-050405bullsgamer,1,4219914.story?coll=cs-bulls-navigation Heat beat Bulls, hard foul by Nocioni] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080521231115/http://chicagosports.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/cs-050405bullsgamer,1,4219914.story?coll=cs-bulls-navigation |date=May 21, 2008 }} Retrieved August 15, 2006</ref>

[[File:Andrés Nocioni.jpg|thumb|left|Andrés Nocioni signing basketballs for fans during his tenure as a Chicago Bull player]]
While giving a [[teleconference]] interview with NBA.com, Nocioni spoke about the hard fouls and his suspension, "First, the one with Wade was completely my fault. It was a bad reaction on my part. If I had received any penalties because of it, it would be a fair sanction, but it was not given. However, the sanction set after the game against the Pistons is totally unfair. I see it as a totally real play taken out of context in the game — absolutely nothing happened. It was an accidental blow. Without purposely trying to, I hit him. I apologized on the court. I also asked Carlos Delfino to give my apologies to him, so I don't understand why there is a sanction for something totally normal in a game."<ref name="Teleconference">[http://www.nba.com/bwb/AndresNocioni2005.html Interview with Andres Nocioni] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070422135002/http://www.nba.com/bwb/AndresNocioni2005.html |date=April 22, 2007 }} Retrieved August 15, 2006</ref> In Nocioni's first NBA playoff game, he scored 25 points and grabbed 18 rebounds while playing all 48 minutes. Due to his outstanding play, the sold-out United Center crowd in Chicago chanted his name. This game solidified Nocioni's status as a Chicago favorite.<ref name="BullsWiz">[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A14187-2005Apr24.html Washington Post article on Bulls-Wizards game] Retrieved August 15, 2006</ref>

In Nocioni's second season with the Chicago Bulls, he averaged 13.0 ppg, 6.1 rpg, and 1.4 apg, while  playing in all 82 games, 43 of them starts. Nocioni was named the Chicago Bulls' Player of the Year for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]].<ref name="POY">[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/nocioni_poy_060419.html Nocioni named Bulls POY] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060825092840/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/nocioni_poy_060419.html |date=August 25, 2006 }} Retrieved August 10, 2006</ref> In [[2006 NBA Playoffs|the playoffs]] Nocioni averaged 22.8 points, 9.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists including two [[double-double]]s. In game two against the [[Miami Heat]] he scored 30 points shooting 13–15 overall from the field (83.3%), including 3–3 in from the three-point line and 1–1 in free throws, with 6 rebounds and one steal in almost 40 minutes played. Nocioni scored 30 points again on November 19, during the 82–72 defeat against the [[L.A. Lakers]].<ref name="YS">[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/boxscore?gid=2006111913 Bulls-Lakers boxscore] Retrieved November 11, 2006</ref>  He also scored a career high 31 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in the December 1st 111–108 road victory against the [[New Orleans Hornets|Hornets]].<ref name="NbaBS">[http://www.nba.com/games/20061201/CHINOK/boxscore.html?nav=scoreboardhome NBA game statistics] Retrieved December 4, 2006</ref> Nocioni missed a third of the [[2006–07 NBA season]] due to [[plantar fasciitis]]. He returned to action late in the season on April 8, 2007, against [[Toronto Raptors|Toronto]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-04-08 |title=Controlling win over Bulls pushes Raptors toward No. 2 seed |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270408028 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024113047/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270408028 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 24, 2012 |access-date=2013-05-02 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Nocioni became a restricted free-agent following the 2006–07 season.  On July 6, 2007, he agreed a 5-year deal with the Chicago Bulls worth a reported $38 million.  Teams that were interested in Nocioni included the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. The deal became official on July 18, 2007.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/nocioni_resigned_070718.html Bulls resign Nocioni to multi-year extension] July 18, 2007</ref> In preparation for the [[2008–09 NBA season]], Nocioni admitted the [[tendinitis|knee tendinitis]] which had hampered his performance during the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Olympics]] was still affecting him and specifically he had hardly done anything in between winning the bronze medal and reporting for training camp.<ref>[http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/chi-14-bulls-chicagooct14,0,1340969.story Andres Nocioni "not in my best shape"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081017011628/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/chi-14-bulls-chicagooct14,0,1340969.story |date=October 17, 2008 }} Retrieved October 28, 2008</ref>

On February 18, 2009, Nocioni was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] along with [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]] and [[Cedric Simmons]] for [[John Salmons]] and [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings_press_release0209.html |title=Kings acquire four players in three-team trade|work=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 18, 2009 |access-date=2009-02-19| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090222171005/http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings_press_release0209.html| archive-date= February 22, 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref> Nocioni started for the Kings the last 23 games of the 2008–09 season, averaging 13.7 points a game.  Sacramento was in a rebuilding process however, and Nocioni requested a trade following a decrease in playing time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoopsworld.com/nba-pm-nocioni-wants-out |title=NBA PM: Nocioni Wants Out | HOOPSWORLD | Basketball News & NBA Rumors |publisher=Hoopsworld |date=2010-06-10 |access-date=2013-05-02}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers===
After the season ended, on June 17, 2010, Nocioni was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] along with [[Spencer Hawes]] for [[Samuel Dalembert]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/100617_trade.html |title=Sixers announce three-player trade with Kings |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 17, 2010 |access-date=2010-06-18| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100619051943/http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/100617_trade.html| archive-date= June 19, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> On December 29, 2010, he scored a season-high 22 points to go along with 12 rebounds, in a 123–110 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].

===Return to Argentina===
During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Nocioni trained with [[Peñarol de Mar del Plata]] while waiting for the situation to resolve itself. With the announcement of the [[National Basketball Players Association|NBPA]] to dissolve the Union and start litigation against the NBA, he agreed to join the team for the [[:es:Torneo Súper 8|Súper 8 tournament]] in November 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ole.com.ar/basquet/ahora-podra-ganarle_0_590941277.html |title=¿Y ahora quién podrá ganarle? |work=www.ole.com.ar |date=November 14, 2011 |access-date=2011-11-15|language=es|publisher=Olé |author1=Olé }}</ref> On November 26, as the NBA announced that a tentative agreement on a new [[collective bargaining agreement]] was reached, Nocioni helped Peñarol to its third Súper 8 tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ole.com.ar/basquet/Vuelta-vuelta_0_598740121.html |title=Vuelta y vuelta |work=www.ole.com.ar |date=November 26, 2011 |access-date=2011-11-29|language=es|publisher=Olé}}</ref>

===Return to Spain===
[[File:Andrés Nocioni 6 Real Madrid Baloncesto Euroleague 20161201 (5).jpg|thumb|150px|Nocioni warming up with Real Madrid in 2016]]
With the end of the lockout, Nocioni returned to the Philadelphia 76ers for the [[2011–12 NBA season]], but was waived in March 2012, after playing 11 games that season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/120320-andres-nocioni-waived.html |title=Sixers Waive Andres Nocioni - 3/20/2012 |work=Nba.com |access-date=2013-05-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209015900/http://www.nba.com/sixers/120320-andres-nocioni-waived.html |archive-date=December 9, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

Nocioni's final NBA game was played on March 12, 2012, in a 103–71 win over the [[Boston Celtics]] where he recorded 1 point and no other stats in 3 and half minutes of playing time.

He then signed with his former team, [[Saski Baskonia|Caja Laboral]] (formerly known as TAU Cerámica for sponsorship reasons), for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ole.com.ar/basquet/Chapu-canta-Vitoria_0_668933391.html |title=Chapu canta Vitoria |work=www.ole.com.ar |date=March 23, 2012 |access-date=2012-03-28|language=es|publisher=Olé |author1=Olé }}</ref> He chose to wear number 55, as number 5, was already taken by his [[Argentina national basketball team]] teammate [[Pablo Prigioni]]. He re-signed with Caja Laboral in July 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/98812/7224/caja-laboral-re-signs-nocioni |title=CAJA LABORAL re-signs Nocioni |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=2012-07-19 |access-date=2013-05-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120827171320/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/98812/7224/caja-laboral-re-signs-nocioni |archive-date=August 27, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 20, 2014, he parted ways with Baskonia,<ref>{{cite news|title=Baskonia, Andres Nocioni officially part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/128180/baskonia-andres-nocioni-officially-part-ways.html|access-date=20 July 2014|work=Sportando.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140723012430/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/128180/baskonia-andres-nocioni-officially-part-ways.html|archive-date=July 23, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> and he signed a two-year contract with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], five days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138606/180|title=Real Madrid makes Nocioni its first new addition|publisher=Euroleague.net|date=2014-07-25| access-date=2014-07-25}}</ref> In May 2015, Real Madrid won the [[2014–15 Euroleague|EuroLeague]], after defeating [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], by a score of 78–59 in [[2015 EuroLeague Final Four|the final game]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is Euroleague champion for record ninth time!|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=251&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=18 July 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> Nocioni was named the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP|Final Four MVP]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Nocioni named bwin MVP of Euroleague Final Four|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5yltk4drkbpxee7j/nocioni-named-bwin-mvp-of-euroleague-final-four|access-date=18 July 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> Real Madrid eventually finished the season winning the [[2014–15 ACB season|Spanish League]] championship, after a 3–0 series sweep in the [[2015 ACB Finals|Spanish League finals series]] against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]]. With that trophy, Real Madrid won the [[European Basketball Triple Crown|triple crown]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid make it 4 out of 4|url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/06/24/en/football/real_madrid/1435176357.html|access-date=24 June 2015|work=marca.com|date=24 June 2015|language=es}}</ref>

On July 21, 2016, Nocioni re-signed with Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid, Nocioni agree to new deal|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73nq6hpymovjjsp7|access-date=21 July 2016|work=Euroleague.net|date=21 July 2016}}</ref> On April 3, 2017, he announced his intentions to retire after the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=EuroLeague icon Andres Nocioni announces retirement|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7pu5ykywnii3wgnq|website=EuroLeague.net|access-date=April 3, 2017|language=en|date=April 3, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nocioni announces his retirement from basketball|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/04/nocioni-announces-his-retirement-from-basketball|website=Real Madrid C.F.|access-date=April 3, 2017|language=en|date=April 3, 2017}}</ref>

==National team career==
Nocioni was called up to defend [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]] and won the silver medal at the 1999 [[South American Basketball Championship|South American Championship]].<ref name="CABB">[http://www.cabb.com.ar/pagadicpub.asp?id=73 Nocioni's profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110527181407/http://www.cabb.com.ar/pagadicpub.asp?id=73 |date=May 27, 2011 }} at the [[Argentine Basketball Federation]]. Retrieved August 16, 2006</ref> In 2001, Nocioni defended Argentina and won the gold medal at the South American Championship.<ref name="CABB" /> and at the [[2001 Tournament of the Americas|2001 FIBA Americas Championship]]. In 2002, Nocioni defended Argentina with distinction and making basketball history. Argentina would beat the [[United States national basketball team|United States]] team, the first team to do so after [[NBA]] players were allowed to compete at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]], in [[Indianapolis, Indiana|Indianapolis]], U.S. The championship would go in the finals to [[FR Yugoslavia national basketball team|Yugoslavia]], Argentina brought home a silver medal.

In 2004, Nocioni was a key factor when Argentina became the first [[Latin American]] team (and the fourth team ever, after the [[United States national basketball team|USA]], [[Yugoslavia national basketball team|Yugoslavia]], and the [[Soviet Union national basketball team|USSR]]) in [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympic]] basketball history, to win the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Olympic gold medal]].

[[File:Bosh vs Argentina.jpg|thumb|170px|Nocioni (#13) defending Chris Bosh, USA v Argentina in August 2008]]
In 2006, Nocioni started for Argentina at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. In a game against [[Venezuela national basketball team|Venezuela]], he landed on an opponent's foot, and it looked he injured his ankle, though he was cleared to play in Argentina's next game against [[Nigeria national basketball team|Nigeria]].<ref name="FIBA">[http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/news/lateNews/FE_news_lateNews_arti.asp?newsID=15751&lid_6720_playerNumber=&lid_6720_teamNumber=&lid_6720_zone=&eventID=3507&roundID=3507&lid_7076_searchForNews=1&lid_7076_searchForPhotos=1&lid_7076_searchForPlayers=1&lid_7076_searchForTeams=1&searchStr=Andr%E9s%20Nocioni Daily review of Group A, FIBA WC 2006]{{dead link|date=September 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Retrieved August 16, 2006</ref> In Argentina's game against Nigeria, Nocioni led the team in scoring, with 23 points, playing 18 minutes, while not missing a single shot. Nocioni was 9–9 from the field, including 5–5 from the 3-point line. "I don't think I've ever played a game where I didn't miss a shot - at least not for the national team."<ref name="FIBA2">[http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/news/lateNews/FE_news_lateNews_arti.asp?newsID=15837&lid_6720_playerNumber=&lid_6720_teamNumber=&lid_6720_zone=&eventID=3507&roundID=3507&lid_7076_searchForNews=1&lid_7076_searchForPhotos=1&lid_7076_searchForPlayers=1&lid_7076_searchForTeams=1&searchStr=Andr%E9s%20Nocioni Game Report, Argentina vs Nigeria 98-64, Group A]{{dead link|date=September 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Retrieved August 16, 2006</ref> Argentina won group A of the tournament, going a perfect 5–0 in the first round of play.<ref name="FIBA3">[http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/news/lateNews/FE_news_lateNews_arti.asp?newsID=15896&lid_6720_playerNumber=&lid_6720_teamNumber=&lid_6720_zone=&eventID=3507&roundID=3507&lid_7076_searchForNews=1&lid_7076_searchForPhotos=1&lid_7076_searchForPlayers=1&lid_7076_searchForTeams=1&searchStr=Andr%E9s%20Nocioni Game Report, Argentina vs Serbia & Montenegro 83-79, Group A]{{dead link|date=September 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Retrieved August 16, 2006</ref>

Argentina lost to [[Spain national basketball team|Spain]] in the 2006 FIBA World Championship semifinal, with a final score of 75–74. Nocioni had a chance to win the game for Argentina, but his [[three-point field goal|three-pointer]] at the end of the game missed, giving Spain the win, and the chance to win the championship.<ref name="FIBA4">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080521165934/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/scheResu/fe_scheStat_gameRepo.asp?roundID=5152&groupName=76&gameName=A&lid_7568_langLC=en&eventID=3507&selNodeID=627&competitionCode=&season=  Game Report, Spain vs Argentina, 75-74, Semi-Final] Retrieved September 2, 2006</ref> Nocioni's Argentine team next played the [[United States national basketball team|US team]] in the bronze medal game, which Argentina lost 96–81. Nocioni scored 18 points in this game, in which he played against [[NBA]] teammate [[Kirk Hinrich]].<ref name="FIBA5">[https://web.archive.org/web/20071101054240/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/scheResu/fe_scheStat_gameRepo.asp?roundID=5154&groupName=79&gameName=A&eventID=3507&lid_7186_openNodeIDs=&langLC=en  Game Report, United States vs Argentina, Bronze Medal Game 96-81] Retrieved September 2, 2006</ref>

In 2008, Nocioni was selected to play with Argentina in the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Beijing Summer Olympics]]. Argentina advanced to the quarter-final with four wins, placing behind [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]] in the group stage, after defeating [[Russia national basketball team|Russia]]. In the game against Russia, Nocioni hit 4 three-pointers, finishing with 19 points.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080920103755/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olym/men/news/gameRepo/p/newsid/28211/repo.html ARG/RUS – Maradona cheers on Manu, Argentina in win over Russia] Retrieved October 28, 2008</ref> After defeating [[Greek national basketball team|Greece]] in the quarterfinals, the Argentine team lost their Olympic semifinals rematch from 4 years earlier against the [[United States national basketball team|US team]]. Due to [[Tendinitis|knee tendinitis]],<ref>[http://www.ole.clarin.com/notas/2008/08/22/basquet/01743487.html Esta vez no alcanzó] [[Diario Olé]] {{in lang|es}}</ref> Nocioni only played 18 minutes, scoring 10 points, and securing 4 rebounds.<ref name="stat">[https://web.archive.org/web/20120405080048/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olym/men/teamPlay/play/p/competitioncode//eventid/4004/fixeddate//langid//langlc/en/season//teamnumber//roundid/6454/playernumber/30397/opponentteamnumber/237/opponentplayernumber/22703/fe_teamPlay_playStat.html Andrés Nocioni player statistics in 2008 Summer Olympics] Retrieved October 28, 2008</ref> Argentina next played [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]], in the bronze medal match, which Argentina won 87–75.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120405080132/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/08/olym/men/news/gameRepo/p/newsid/28368/repo.html ARG/LTU – Unheralded Gutierrez, Quinteros shine as Argentina win bronze] Retrieved October 28, 2008</ref> Nocioni scored 14 points in that game.<ref name="stat" />

In 2011, he was a part of the team that won the gold medal in the [[2011 FIBA Americas Championship]], that was played in Mar del Plata. He also played at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]], and the [[2015 FIBA Americas Championship]], where he won a silver medal, and was named to the [[FIBA AmeriCup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. He finished his national team career by playing at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/andres%20nocioni/pid//_//players.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110530100514/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp/q/Andres%20Nocioni/pid/_/players.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 30, 2011 |title=Andrés NOCIONI (ARG) participated in 14 FIBA / FIBA Zones events. |website=archive.fiba.com}}</ref>

On February 26, 2018, the [[Argentine Basketball Confederation]] retired the #13 jersey worn by Nocioni during his career with the national team. The ceremony was held in the Parque Carlos Guerrero stadium of [[Olavarría]] during the Argentina v. [[Paraguay national basketball team|Paraguay]] match for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)|2019 World Cup qualification]].<ref name=thirteen>[https://www.lanacion.com.ar/2112420-eliminatorias-de-basquetbol-rumbo-a-china-2019-un-emotivo-homenaje-en-el-retiro-de-la-camiseta-de-andres-nocioni El retiro de la camiseta N° 13 de Andrés Nocioni: el homenaje en Olavarría al "alma" de la Generación Dorada] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316004547/https://www.lanacion.com.ar/2112420-eliminatorias-de-basquetbol-rumbo-a-china-2019-un-emotivo-homenaje-en-el-retiro-de-la-camiseta-de-andres-nocioni |date=March 16, 2018 }}, ''La Nación'', 26 Feb 2018</ref>

Nocioni was also appointed as collaborator of the Argentina coaching staff.<ref>[https://www.clarin.com/deportes/basquet/retiraron-camiseta-nocioni_0_rkVoJgz_z.html Retiraron la camiseta N°13 del Chapu Nocioni en la Selección], ''Clarín'', 26 Feb 2018</ref>
